about: The storybook both clients are held to: every whole screen a person reaches, in each state that changes how the screen is put together. One piece in one variant (a row kind, an ask card, a message inside an otherwise identical screen) is a component example instead. A story either client lacks says why. The terminal's storybook is crates/shot/src/stories.rs; the phone's stories are examples of apps/apple/Amux/Debug/ComponentCatalog.swift, compared by its component snapshots. Each side's tests check its storybook against this list.

stories.name: fleet.first-run
stories.shows: The agent list on a client paired with nothing yet: what to do first.

stories.name: fleet.first-run-looking
stories.shows: Nothing paired and nothing found yet: still looking, and the two steps on the computer.
stories.why: The terminal does not look for machines from its agent list; machines found nearby show in its hosts window.

stories.name: fleet.first-run-refused
stories.shows: Nothing paired on a phone refused the local network.
stories.why: Only the phone asks for the local network.

stories.name: fleet.first-run-signed-out
stories.shows: Nothing paired on a phone with no account, offering to sign in under pairing.
stories.why: Only the phone has accounts on screen; the terminal signs in with amux login.

stories.name: fleet.first-run-on-the-account-free
stories.shows: Nothing paired on the free plan, with a machine on the account only the relay reaches, offered a subscription in place of a pairing.
stories.why: The terminal does not look for machines from its agent list; the account's machines show in its hosts window.

stories.name: fleet.no-agents
stories.shows: A phone paired with a machine that runs no agents yet.
stories.why: The terminal's agent list reads the same with no agents whether or not machines are paired, as fleet.first-run shows.

stories.name: fleet.busy
stories.shows: A day's agents on several machines, one of them away: agents that need you first, then working, idle, a family, and the exited ones.

stories.name: fleet.filter
stories.shows: The agent list narrowed to the agents whose names match a word.

stories.name: fleet.no-matches
stories.shows: The agent list narrowed to nothing.

stories.name: fleet.signed-out
stories.shows: The busy list on a phone with no account: a hollow person where the account disc would be.
stories.why: Only the phone has accounts on screen; the terminal signs in with amux login.

stories.name: fleet.stop
stories.shows: Stopping a working agent from the agent list: what stopping cuts short, and the confirm.
stories.why: The phone stops an agent from its chat, as chat.stop shows.

stories.name: fleet.delete
stories.shows: Deleting an exited agent and its history from the agent list.
stories.why: The phone deletes an agent from its chat, as chat.delete shows.

stories.name: fleet.rename
stories.shows: Renaming an agent in place on its row in the agent list.
stories.why: The phone renames an agent from its chat, as chat.rename shows.

stories.name: fleet.large-text
stories.shows: The busy list at the largest accessibility text size.
stories.why: The terminal draws every story at each of its sizes instead.

stories.name: hosts.list
stories.shows: Every paired machine, each saying how it is reached, one away, with one found nearby and not paired.

stories.name: hosts.empty
stories.shows: Hosts with no other machine paired or found.

stories.name: hosts.network-refused
stories.shows: Hosts with nothing found because this phone was refused the local network.
stories.why: Only the phone asks for the local network.

stories.name: hosts.on-the-account-free

stories.why: The terminal's hosts window draws every unpaired machine as one line of words, as hosts.list shows; it has no card to sell from.

stories.name: hosts.large-text
stories.shows: Hosts at the largest accessibility text size.
stories.why: The terminal draws every story at each of its sizes instead.

stories.name: host.page
stories.shows: One machine's page: how it is reached, what it runs, its addresses and key.
stories.why: The terminal gives each machine one line in its hosts window, with no page of its own.

stories.why: The terminal pairs with amux pair on its command line.

stories.name: pair.code-checking

stories.why: The terminal pairs with amux pair on its command line.

stories.name: pair.code-refused

stories.why: The terminal pairs with amux pair on its command line.

stories.name: pair.code-subscribe
stories.shows: A code that reached a machine only the relay can carry, on the free plan.
stories.why: The terminal pairs with amux pair on its command line.

stories.shows: New Agent at the largest accessibility text size: every field's value under its label, and the last row clear of the Start bar.

stories.name: chat.signed-out

stories.shows: Changing the agent's model, effort or permission from its chat.

stories.name: chat.stop
stories.shows: Stopping an agent from its chat: the plain confirm.

stories.name: chat.delete

stories.name: chat.large-text
stories.shows: A chat at the largest accessibility text size: the header held at the largest ordinary size, and the step rows stacking verb, subject and counts.

stories.why: The terminal draws every story at each of its sizes instead.

stories.why: The terminal has no settings screen; it is set up with amux on its command line.

stories.name: settings.signed-out
